images.caption: Figure 1:SFT builds a shortcut, and VETO suppresses it.Accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-7B against its text-only accuracy, where a rise indicates the shortcut. (a) Within the training distribution (SSv2) SFT and VETO reach a similar gain in accuracy, but the shortcut grows much more under SFT. (b) Under the shift (Perception Test) VETO gains accuracy whereas SFT gains only the shortcut.

Figure 4:Pipeline of VETO.Calibration, once per VideoLLM, collects the activations of the text-only input at every layer and takes the leading directions of their spectrum as the shortcut subspace. During fine-tuning, the LoRA update is projected off that subspace after each optimizer step, so that the part along the shortcut directions is removed and the rest is kept, whereas SFT keeps both.
